title: U.S. House · California's 33rd District
area: Inland Empire, including Redlands, San Bernardino, Fontana, Rialto, and Colton in San Bernardino County.

context.text: California uses a top-two nonpartisan primary. In the June 2, 2026 primary, Pete Aguilar (D) placed first with 53.5% and Stephanie Vargas (R) placed second with 17.5%, advancing both to the November general election.

candidates.name: Pete Aguilar
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 33rd District (since 2023); previously represented California's 31st District (2015–2023)

summary.text: Pete Aguilar is the Democratic incumbent for California's 33rd Congressional District and has served in the U.S. House since 2015. A former Redlands mayor and local-government staffer, he has chaired the House Democratic Caucus since 2023 and serves on the Appropriations Committee.

background.text: Born in Fontana, California, in 1979. According to his official biography, his family has lived in the community for four generations; he started his first job at age twelve working with his grandfather at the San Bernardino County Courthouse cafeteria.

Graduated from Yucaipa High School and earned bachelor's degrees in government and business administration from the University of Redlands in 2001. His official biography says he put himself through college with student loans and federal grants.
Worked as a business owner and as an executive of a community credit union, then as Deputy Director and later Interim Director of the Inland Empire Regional Office of the California governor.
Appointed to the Redlands City Council in 2006 and served until 2014; he was Mayor of Redlands from 2010 to 2014.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2014 and took office in 2015; most recently re-elected in 2024.
Serves on the House Appropriations Committee and is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and the New Democrat Coalition.
Elected House Democratic Caucus chairman for the 118th Congress on November 30, 2022, and re-elected unopposed for the 119th Congress on November 19, 2024.
His official biography says he lives in Redlands with his wife Alisha and their two sons.

priorities.text: In his 2014 campaign platform, listed building an economy that is 'strong and fair,' improving public education, a 'sound approach to energy and the environment,' protecting Medicare and Social Security, and comprehensive immigration reform as priorities.

positions.summary: Visited Inland Empire health facilities affected by federal Medicaid and Medicare cuts enacted in the 2025 reconciliation law and said he would keep fighting the cuts so families can afford care.
positions.quote: But now, many of the seniors, children, veterans and others who receive care from these centers may no longer be able to afford it thanks to Republican cuts to Medi-Cal and Medicare made in the Big Ugly Bill. I'll keep fighting back against these reckless attacks on lifesaving healthcare programs.

positions.summary: Opposed a floor amendment that would have struck Israel funding from FY2027 appropriations, saying it would compromise national security and peace efforts and abandon allies and agreements, while noting Congress can later review U.S. assistance to Israel.
positions.quote: I believe it's wrong to abandon our allies and walk away from our agreements during such a fragile moment. That is why I opposed this amendment and similarly opposed the Massie amendment to eliminate aid to Jordan.

positions.summary: Toured a local manufacturer hurt by rising costs from tariffs and said he is committed to rolling back what he called reckless tariffs.
positions.quote: I'm committed to working to lower prices, improve California's air quality, roll back reckless tariffs and end the conflict in the Middle East so businesses like Anita's can thrive.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, and H.R. 18, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 4876, the Reproductive Freedom for Veterans Act, which directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to provide abortion care, counseling and related services (119th Congress).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Defense subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).
Serves as chairman of the House Democratic Caucus for the 119th Congress, a leadership post he has held since the 118th Congress.

summary.text: Stephanie Vargas is the Republican candidate for California's 33rd Congressional District, having placed second in the June 2026 top-two primary. A longtime San Bernardino County resident, she works as a city clerk's office official in Colton and describes herself as a Christian. She has been endorsed by the Republican Party of San Bernardino County and is running on issues including cost of living, public safety, and veterans services.

background.text: Says she grew up in San Bernardino and has lived in District 33 her whole life.

According to her iVoterGuide profile, she earned an associate degree in business administration and management from San Bernardino Valley Community College and a certificate through UC Riverside Extension.

Early work history listed on iVoterGuide: San Bernardino Police Department police cadet (2010-2013) and Police Explorer (2009-2012), general manager of a Menchie's in Fontana (2014-2016), and City of Fontana community service assistant (2016-2018).

Has worked for the City of Colton since 2018: administrative assistant (2018-2021), deputy city clerk (2021-2023), acting city clerk (2023-2024), and chief deputy city clerk (2024-2026), per iVoterGuide. A voter guide describes her as a chief deputy clerk.
Lists membership in the International Institute of Municipal Clerks and the California Municipal Clerks Association, and board service at Springs Charter School (2022-2026).

This is her first run for office: iVoterGuide lists no prior political offices held or sought. She placed second in the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary with 17.5% of the vote (20,952 votes) and is endorsed by the Republican Party of San Bernardino County.

priorities.text: Lists supporting law enforcement and fire service personnel, standing up for parental rights, and lowering the cost of living and 'fixing the housing crisis' with tax relief for families and businesses as her three key campaign messages.
priorities.quote: I am committed to supporting our law enforcement and fire service personnel, ensuring our community remains a safe place to live, work, and raise a family. I will fight for our families, stand up for parental rights, and deliver the common-sense policies our children need to thrive. I am stepping up to confront our economic challenges head-on—from lowering the cost of living and fixing the housing crisis to delivering the tax relief our families and businesses desperately need.

researchNotes: Aguilar has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and has no dedicated issues subpages beyond a general community-funding page; his 2026 positions here are drawn from official House press releases on health care, Israel funding, ICE facility conditions, and tariffs. His 2014 platform is cited as background context only. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for both candidates are added separately by script. Stephanie Vargas: no campaign website found (the stephanievargas.com domain belongs to an unrelated person); Ballotpedia was not fetchable; no additional statements added. Biography notes: Vargas has no Ballotpedia biography; her career details come from an iVoterGuide profile and a voter-guide Q&A, not an independent news profile.
